oneOf.description:
Customer user type representing marketplace buyers in the shopping mall platform.

Customers have access to shopping functionality including product browsing, cart management, order placement, and personal account management. This user type is designed for end consumers who purchase products from marketplace sellers.

Customer permissions include:
- Product catalog browsing and search capabilities
- Shopping cart and wishlist management
- Order history and tracking access
- Personal profile and address management
- Product review and rating submission
- Customer support ticket creation

Customers authenticate through dedicated customer registration and login endpoints with email verification requirements. The customer dashboard provides shopping-focused interfaces and personal account management tools.

Seller user type representing marketplace vendors and merchants in the shopping mall platform.

Sellers have comprehensive business management capabilities including product catalog management, inventory control, order fulfillment, and business analytics access. This user type is designed for businesses that sell products through the marketplace.

Seller permissions include:
- Product listing creation and management with bulk operations
- Inventory level management across warehouse locations
- Order fulfillment and shipping management
- Business analytics and sales reporting access
- Customer communication and support interaction
- Financial transaction monitoring and payout management

Sellers authenticate through dedicated seller registration and login endpoints with business verification requirements. The seller dashboard provides business-focused interfaces and operational management tools.

Admin user type representing platform administrators and system operators in the shopping mall platform.

Admins have comprehensive platform management capabilities including user oversight, content moderation, system configuration, and analytics access. This user type is designed for platform staff who manage the marketplace ecosystem.

Admin permissions include:
- User account management across all user types
- Product catalog moderation and approval workflows
- Order management and dispute resolution
- Platform-wide analytics and reporting access
- System configuration and operational parameter control
- Content management and policy enforcement

Admins authenticate through dedicated admin registration and login endpoints with enhanced security requirements. The admin dashboard provides comprehensive platform oversight interfaces and system management tools.

IShoppingMallUserType.description:
User type enumeration defining the different user role types within the shopping mall platform.

This enumeration represents the various user personas and their access levels in the marketplace ecosystem. User types determine authorization boundaries, feature access, and administrative privileges across the platform.

The system supports three distinct user personas:
- Customer accounts for marketplace buyers with shopping, order management, and personal profile capabilities
- Seller accounts for marketplace vendors and merchants with product management, inventory control, and business analytics access
- Admin accounts for platform management and oversight with comprehensive administrative controls and system-wide permissions

Each user type integrates with the JWT-based authentication system and role-based access control (RBAC) implementation. The enumeration drives dashboard routing, API authorization boundaries, and feature visibility throughout the shopping mall platform. User type determination occurs during registration and login processes, with specific authentication flows for each persona.

IShoppingMallProductImage.description:
Product images representing visual assets for product display in the shopping mall marketplace.

Product images serve as the primary visual representation for products in the catalog, supporting multiple images per product with display hierarchy and metadata tracking. Images are essential for customer purchase decisions and are optimized for performance across different devices and page contexts.

Images support full lifecycle management from upload to archival, with automatic format optimization and CSS sizing for optimal storefront presentation. Each image maintains quality settings and can be tagged for different display contexts like main product showcases, thumbnails, or promotional materials.

The image system supports complex display hierarchies with primary image designation, sequential display ordering, and accessibility features including alternative text and captioning. All images are timestamped for lifecycle tracking and support real-time updates to maintain catalog accuracy across the marketplace platform.

id.description: Primary key identifier for the product image record. Generated automatically upon image upload and serves as the unique reference throughout the platform.

product_id.description: Foreign key reference to the parent product entity. Links the image to a specific product in the shopping mall catalog for display attribution and management.

image_url.description: Absolute file path or URL to the stored image asset. Points to the optimized image file location within the platform's content delivery network for performance-optimized delivery.

alt_text.description: Accessibility text for screen readers and alternative display contexts. Describes the image content for users who cannot view images and ensures ADA compliance.

display_order.description: Sequential display ordering position within the product's image collection. Determines the visual presentation sequence in product galleries and catalog listings.

is_primary.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this image serves as the primary display image for the product. Primary images are featured in catalog browsing and search result displays.

caption.description: Optional descriptive caption providing additional context about the image. Used in detailed product views and can enhance customer understanding of product features shown in the image.

created_at.description: Timestamp of image record creation in the platform. Represents when the image was first associated with the product and uploaded to the catalog system.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent image record modification. Tracks when display settings, captions, or other metadata were last updated for audit purposes.

IShoppingMallProductReviewStatistics.description:
Product review statistics aggregating customer feedback metrics for comprehensive seller analytics and customer decision support within the shopping mall platform.

Review statistics provide quantified assessment of product quality and customer satisfaction through aggregated rating scores, review volume analysis, and helpfulness metrics. These statistics serve as key performance indicators for sellers to understand customer perception and identify improvement opportunities while helping customers make informed purchase decisions based on collective feedback.

Statistics are computed in real-time across all approved reviews and include comprehensive metrics such as average ratings, review distribution patterns, temporal trend analysis, and engagement quality indicators. The statistics help identify common customer concerns, highlight product strengths, and guide inventory and service decisions within the broader marketplace analytics ecosystem.

These aggregated metrics form the foundation of the review system credibility, enabling sophisticated ranking algorithms and personalized recommendations while maintaining transparency in customer satisfaction measurement and enabling data-driven business optimization for marketplace sellers.

id.description: Primary key identifier for the review statistics record. Generated automatically upon statistics creation and serves as the unique reference for tracking aggregation lifecycle.

shopping_product_id.description: Foreign key reference to the product entity being analyzed. Links the statistics to a specific catalog item for accurate review attribution and analytics correlation.

total_reviews.description: Total count of approved reviews contributing to these statistics. Represents the sample size for rating calculations and provides context for statistical significance of averaged metrics.

average_rating.description: Arithmetic mean of all valid review ratings on a 5-star scale. The primary quality indicator calculated from aggregated customer satisfaction scores across all approved reviews.

five_star_count.description: Count of reviews awarding the maximum 5-star rating. Indicates exceptional customer satisfaction and product quality excellence within the review dataset.

four_star_count.description: Count of reviews awarding 4-star ratings. Represents high but not perfect customer satisfaction and typically indicates products meeting or exceeding expectations with minor considerations.

three_star_count.description: Count of reviews awarding 3-star ratings. Indicates average customer satisfaction and typically represents products meeting basic expectations but lacking exceptional qualities.

two_star_count.description: Count of reviews awarding 2-star ratings. Represents below-average customer satisfaction and often highlights significant product issues or unmet customer expectations.

one_star_count.description: Count of reviews awarding the minimum 1-star rating. Indicates severe customer dissatisfaction and typically signals major product defects, misleading descriptions, or quality failures.

last_calculation_at.description: Timestamp when review statistics were last recalculated and updated. Tracks the freshness of statistical metrics and triggers re-computation based on new review submissions or aggregated changes.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the statistics record was initially created in the platform. Represents the first calculation of review statistics for this product and provides baseline creation context.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent statistics record modification. Tracks when review counts, rating calculations, or statistical properties were last updated for audit trail purposes.

IShoppingMallInventoryStatus.description:
Inventory status utility type without database coupling.

This type represents standardized inventory status information used for inventory management workflows within the shopping mall platform. Since no corresponding Prisma database model exists, this schema serves as an interface-only type without direct database persistence.

Common inventory statuses might include in-stock, low-stock, out-of-stock, and discontinued conditions. However, without an underlying database model, this type should only be used for API interface purposes where business logic anticipates inventory status processing but does not require direct database field mapping.

This approach ensures API design flexibility while maintaining consistency with the actual database schema available in the shopping mall platform. Any future inventory status implementation would need corresponding database model creation before schema fields can be defined.

text: Perfect! Now I'll create the comprehensive E2E test functions for your e-commerce platform. Let me generate the test suites for all the API endpoints.

instruction:
Create comprehensive E2E test suites for the e-commerce shopping mall platform covering the following areas:

Authentication & User Management Tests:
- User registration with various input scenarios (valid/invalid email, password strength, duplicate accounts)
- Login functionality including JWT token validation and session management
- Password reset flow with email verification
- User profile updates including address management scenarios
- Role-based access control testing for different user types

Product Catalog Tests:
- Product listing with pagination, search, and filtering across multiple criteria
- Product detail retrieval including variant information (SKU) validation
- Category navigation and hierarchical browsing
- Advanced search functionality and result relevance
- Product availability and inventory status checking

Shopping Features Tests:
- Shopping cart operations (add, update quantity, remove items)
- Cart persistence and session management
- Wishlist functionality with product management
- Product variant selection and inventory validation
- Cart checkout flow with various scenarios

Order Management Tests:
- Order creation from cart with different product combinations
- Order status transitions (pending → processing → shipped → delivered)
- Order history retrieval and filtering
- Payment processing integration with various payment methods
- Order cancellation requests and refund processing
- Inventory updates during order placement and cancellation

Seller Dashboard Tests:
- Seller account creation and profile management
- Product CRUD operations with bulk operations
- Product variant (SKU) management and inventory tracking
- Order fulfillment process and status updates
- Seller analytics and reporting accuracy

Review System Tests:
- Product review submission with rating validation
- Review management (edit, delete) functionality
- Rating aggregation and display accuracy
- Review filtering and sorting capabilities

Admin Dashboard Tests:
- Comprehensive dashboard data accuracy
- User management operations (view, suspend, modify roles)
- Product moderation and approval workflows
- Order management and monitoring capabilities
- Platform-wide statistics validation

Integration & Data Flow Tests:
- End-to-end purchase flow from product browsing to delivery
- Multi-user scenarios (concurrent shopping, inventory conflicts)
- Payment integration with simulated transactions
- Email notification systems for key events
- File upload functionality for product images and user avatars

Edge Cases & Error Handling:
- Concurrent product purchases and inventory conflicts
- User account security scenarios (brute force protection, session hijacking)
- Data validation and sanitization across all endpoints
- Rate limiting and API throttling scenarios
- Network failures and recovery mechanisms

Security & Performance Tests:
- Authentication bypass attempts and security validation
- SQL injection prevention and XSS protection
- API response time validation for critical user flows
- Load testing consideration for peak shopping seasons

scenario.draft: Test guest registration with only required fields to validate minimum data requirements. Verifies successful session creation when only href, referrer, session_id, user_agent, and timestamp fields are provided, with optional IP address omitted. Ensures the system handles minimal guest data appropriately while maintaining security and session functionality. Tests that required timestamp fields (created_at, updated_at, last_activity_at) are properly handled.

Test guest registration with IPv6 address format instead of IPv4. Validates that the system correctly handles both IPv4 and IPv6 IP address formats for guest session tracking. Ensures proper IP address storage and validation for modern network environments, particularly for mobile and IPv6-enabled networks. Verifies that IPv6 addresses are accepted without causing validation errors or data parsing issues.

Test guest registration with mobile device user agent strings to validate device detection and compatibility. Uses typical mobile browser user agents (iPhone, Android devices) to ensure proper session establishment for mobile shoppers. Validates that mobile users can successfully create guest sessions and that the system properly captures device characteristics for analytics and compatibility verification.

Test guest registration with various referrer scenarios including direct access, search engine referrals, and social media traffic. Validates handling of different referrer types including search engines (google.com, bing.com), social platforms (facebook.com, instagram.com), and email campaigns. Ensures accurate traffic source attribution for marketing analytics and conversion tracking purposes.

Test guest registration with edge cases in session ID generation including very short session IDs and maximum length boundaries. Validates minimum length requirement of 10 characters and maximum length of 64 characters for session identifier validation. Tests handling of exactly at boundary limits and just outside acceptable ranges to ensure proper validation mechanisms function correctly.

Test guest registration with invalid URI formats in href and referrer fields to validate input sanitization and error handling. Tests malformed URLs, missing protocols, invalid characters, and edge cases that could potentially cause security vulnerabilities. Ensures proper validation and error messaging when invalid data formats are submitted during guest session creation attempts.

Test password reset with missing email parameter to validate proper error handling and validation messages. This scenario ensures the API correctly identifies and responds to missing required fields in the password reset request. The test confirms that appropriate validation errors are returned and no security tokens are generated for invalid requests.

Test password reset with invalid email format (missing @, malformed format, special characters) to validate email validation rules. This scenario ensures the API properly validates email format requirements and provides clear error messages for malformed email addresses. The test covers various invalid email formats commonly entered by users accidentally.

Test password reset request for an email address that doesn't exist in the system database. This validates that the API handles user enumeration protection by following security best practices. The test confirms that the API provides consistent responses whether the email exists or not, preventing attackers from determining valid user accounts through the password reset interface.

Test successful multi-factor authentication verification using a valid TOTP (Time-based One-Time Password) code. This scenario validates the complete MFA verification flow for enhanced account security, ensuring proper JWT token generation and session establishment after successful 6-digit code validation. The test should verify successful token response with proper access_token, token_type, and expires_in fields, confirming the authentication flow works correctly for secure platform access.

Test multi-factor authentication verification failure when providing an invalid or expired TOTP code. This scenario validates proper error handling and security measures for incorrect verification attempts, ensuring the system properly rejects invalid authentication codes. The test should verify appropriate error responses and maintain account security by not granting access with incorrect verification codes, protecting against unauthorized access attempts.

Test multi-factor authentication verification failure when the authentication session has expired or is invalid. This scenario validates proper session management and timeout handling, ensuring MFA verification requires valid session context. The test should verify appropriate error responses when session_id references an expired or non-existent authentication session, maintaining security through proper session lifecycle management.

Test multi-factor authentication verification replay attack protection by attempting to reuse a previously valid TOTP code. This scenario validates time-sensitive code validation and replay prevention mechanisms, ensuring each verification code can only be used once within its valid time window. The test should verify proper rejection of reused codes and maintain the integrity of the MFA system against replay attacks while preserving user security.

Test multi-factor authentication verification rate limiting protection by simulating multiple failed verification attempts. This scenario validates brute force attack prevention mechanisms, ensuring the system properly implements rate limiting to protect against unauthorized access attempts. The test should verify appropriate throttling responses after multiple consecutive failures, demonstrating comprehensive security measures that balance user convenience with security protection.

Test multi-factor authentication verification with various code formatting edge cases including leading zeros, whitespace handling, and non-numeric inputs. This scenario validates robust input handling and sanitization, ensuring the system properly processes different code formats while maintaining security integrity. The test should verify appropriate handling of formatted inputs and maintain strict validation standards for authentication code processing.

Test successful admin token refresh functionality where a valid refresh token is used to obtain new access and refresh tokens. This scenario validates the complete refresh flow including proper token validation, authentication renewal, and maintaining administrative privileges across session extensions. Should verify that new tokens are properly generated with correct expiration times and that the admin continues to have full dashboard access after refresh.

Test admin refresh failure when an invalid or malformed refresh token is provided. This scenario verifies proper error handling for token validation failures including appropriate error responses and ensuring no new tokens are issued when the refresh token cannot be validated. Should ensure the system maintains security by rejecting fake or tampered tokens without revealing sensitive information about why validation failed.

Test admin refresh failure when attempting to use an expired refresh token. This scenario validates the system's ability to detect expired tokens beyond their refreshable_until timestamp and properly handle scenarios where token renewal is no longer possible. Validates that users are directed back to login when their refresh capability has expired while maintaining audit trail for failed renewal attempts.

Test admin refresh request when the refresh token field is missing from the request payload. This scenario validates proper validation of required fields and ensures the API returns appropriate validation errors instead of processing malformed requests. Should verify that missing required fields trigger validation errors with helpful error messaging without exposing internal system implementation details.

Test admin authentication failure with incorrect email or password. Verify that the system rejects invalid credentials while maintaining security by not revealing whether the email exists or if the password was incorrect. Ensure no authentication tokens are returned and appropriate error responses are provided for both email not found and password mismatch scenarios.

Test admin authentication attempt with an inactive administrator account. Verify that authentication fails when is_active status is false, ensuring inactive administrators cannot access the platform management system. Validate that appropriate access denied responses are returned while maintaining account security.

Test admin authentication attempt with a deleted administrator account. Verify that authentication fails when deleted_at timestamp is present, ensuring former administrators cannot access administrative functions. Validate proper handling of soft-deleted accounts while maintaining audit trail integrity.

Test admin authentication with invalid email format. Verify that authentication fails when email does not meet RFC 5322 standards as specified in the IShoppingMallAdmin.ILogin schema. Validate proper email format validation while maintaining security by not revealing whether an invalid format matches any existing accounts.

Test admin authentication for super administrator accounts with is_super_admin status true. Verify that super administrators receive elevated permissions and unrestricted platform access as indicated by the is_super_admin field in IShoppingMallAdmin.IAuthorized response. Validate comprehensive platform management capabilities are properly authenticated and authorized.

Test admin authentication for department-level administrators. Verify that administrators with department assignments receive appropriate scoped permissions within their organizational units. Confirm that the department field in IShoppingMallAdmin.IAuthorized properly reflects assignment while maintaining role-based access control boundaries.

Test comprehensive audit trail generation during admin authentication including IP tracking, referrer monitoring, and session context capture as defined in IShoppingMallAdmin.ILogin schema. Verify that authentication attempts are properly logged with href and referrer URLs for administrative access pattern analysis and security monitoring.

Test JWT token generation and serialization for administrative sessions. Verify that access and refresh tokens are properly formatted according to IAuthorizationToken schema with correct expiration timestamps in ISO 8601 format. Validate token structure, expiration controls, and refresh token lifecycle management for administrative session security.

Test successful refresh of seller's access token using a valid refresh token. Validates token renewal maintains business session continuity and updates JWT tokens with new expiration timestamps, ensuring uninterrupted dashboard access during active business operations.
Test error handling when attempting to refresh using a revoked or blacklisted refresh token. Ensures systems properly track revoked sessions and prevent unauthorized access using compromised tokens.

Test customer verification email resend succeeds when customer provides valid email address for account verification. Validates resend mechanism during registration process, ensures fresh verification token generation, cites email service provider success, and confirms system allows customer verification retry within rate limited timeframe.

Test system enforces rate limiting rules by restricting frequent verification resend request. Shows that sequential multiple requests within short timeframe return appropriate warnings and timestamps suggesting cooling-off period, ensuring protection against email delivery abuse.

Test system correctly handles optional IP tracking for security monitoring during verification resend. Demonstrates the mechanism stores client IP address when provided for audit trail and controls against bot traffic, while allowing tolerance for cases where client can't determine IP (SSR contexts).

Test successful email verification using a six-digit numeric verification code. This scenario validates the complete email verification flow where a customer receives a verification code via email and successfully confirms their email address. The test should verify that entering a valid 6-digit code (matching the pattern ^[0-9]{6}$) successfully activates the customer account, returns a success response with customerId, and sets the proper verification timestamp. This ensures the email verification system works correctly for code-based verification method and properly activates customer accounts in the shopping mall platform.

Test successful email verification using a UUID-based verification token from email links. This scenario validates the token-based verification method where customers click verification links in their email containing a UUID token. The test should verify that submitting a valid UUID token successfully verifies the email address, activates the customer account, and returns proper confirmation response with customerId and verification timestamp. This ensures the one-click email verification workflow functions correctly and provides a seamless user experience for email confirmation in the shopping mall platform.

Test email verification failure with invalid verification code format. This scenario validates proper error handling when users submit verification codes that don't match the required six-digit numeric pattern (^[0-9]{6}$). The test should verify that codes with wrong length, non-numeric characters, or incorrect format are rejected with appropriate error messages. This ensures the verification system properly validates code format and provides clear feedback to users about format requirements for the shopping mall email verification process.

Test email verification failure with expired verification code. This scenario validates proper handling of expired verification codes (codes expire after 15 minutes for security purposes). The test should verify that attempting to verify with an expired code returns appropriate error response indicating the code has expired and suggesting users request a new verification email. This ensures the verification system enforces security time limits and provides helpful guidance for users with expired verification codes in the shopping mall platform.

Test email verification failure with expired verification token. This scenario validates proper handling of expired verification tokens (tokens expire after 24 hours from generation). The test should verify that attempting to verify with an expired UUID token returns appropriate error response indicating the token has expired and suggesting users request a new verification email. This ensures the token-based verification system enforces security time limits and provides helpful guidance for users with expired verification tokens in the shopping mall platform.

Test email verification attempt on an already verified email address. This scenario validates proper handling when users try to verify an email address that has already been successfully verified. The test should verify that the system returns appropriate response indicating the email is already verified, preventing duplicate verification attempts and maintaining data integrity. This ensures the verification system properly tracks verification status and prevents unnecessary verification attempts for already active accounts in the shopping mall platform.

Test session validation for anonymous guest users. Validates the authentication system properly handles guest sessions, returning appropriate guest user context and temporary access permissions. Confirms guest sessions maintain anonymous browsing capabilities while tracking necessary session data.

Test comprehensive session cleanup including temporary data removal and cached information clearing. Validates the sessionCleanup flag functionality to perform thorough session termination beyond basic token invalidation. Ensures all session artifacts are properly removed including shopping cart data, navigation preferences, and temporary file operations.

Test logout behavior with malformed, expired, or invalid JWT tokens. Validates proper error handling when tokens don't match expected format pattern '^[A-Za-z0-9-_]+\.[A-Za-z0-9-_]+\.[A-Za-z0-9-_]+$'. Ensures graceful failure with appropriate error messages while maintaining security audit trails for invalid token attempts.

Test comprehensive validation of successful logout response structure. Validates all required response fields: success (boolean), message (string), timestamp (ISO 8601 format), sessionId (UUID format), and userType (customer/seller/admin/guest). Ensures response completeness and data type accuracy while maintaining API contract consistency across different user contexts.

Test customer login with invalid email format to verify email validation enforcement. Ensure system rejects malformed email addresses like 'invalid-email' or 'user@' and returns appropriate validation error messages. Validate that no authentication tokens are generated for malformed email inputs.

Test customer login with incorrect password to verify authentication failure. Ensure system rejects invalid credentials without revealing whether email exists, maintains account security, and prevents unauthorized access. Validate proper error messaging without credential enumeration vulnerability.

Test customer login with non-existent email address to verify proper authentication failure handling. Ensure system responds consistently for non-existent accounts and prevents user enumeration attacks. Validate that no authentication tokens are issued and appropriate error responses are returned.

Test customer login with empty or missing credentials to verify required field validation. Ensure system properly validates required email and password fields without authentication processing. Validate that missing field validation occurs before authentication attempts.

Test basic product catalog browsing with default parameters. Validates that customers can successfully browse the marketplace with basic pagination settings. This fundamental test ensures the core catalog accessibility works, including price display validation, seller information verification, and basic search result formatting. The customer should be able to load the first page of products to begin their shopping journey.

Test comprehensive pagination navigation through product catalog results. Verifies customers can browse through multiple pages of products with different item counts per page. This covers forward/backward navigation, page boundary conditions, and result consistency. Validates navigation from page 1 to page 2 with different limits (10, 20 items) to ensure customers can discover products systematically across the entire catalog.

Test product discovery through natural language text search queries. This validates the marketplace's search engine functionality by searching across product names, descriptions, and tags. Covers common shopping scenarios like searching for 'laptop computer', 'summer dress', or 'wireless headphones'. The search should return relevant products matching customer intent for various product categories from electronics to fashion.

Test hierarchical category browsing and navigation within specific product categories. Validates the taxonomy system by exploring categories like 'Electronics', 'Fashion', or 'Home & Garden'. This covers navigation through different levels of categorization where customers drill down from broad categories to more specific subcategories for targeted product discovery.

Test customer browsing of products from specific marketplace sellers. Validates that customers can view all products from preferred or trusted sellers they follow. This enables customer loyalty and reduces marketplace competition by maintaining seller-customer relationships. The system should return products only from the specified seller ID while maintaining proper filtering and pagination.

Test product availability filtering to show only products currently available for purchase. This validates that customers can filter out out-of-stock items during their shopping experience. Covers scenarios where customers want to see only 'in_stock' products or specifically 'backorder_allowed' items for preorder or special ordering scenarios.

Test all available product sorting options including price directions, popularity ratings, newest arrivals, and relevance scoring. Validates marketplace UX by ensuring customers can sort results according to their preference for better product discovery. Covers sorting by 'price_low_to_high' for budget-conscious shopping and 'rating' for quality-first decisions among other options.

Test product discovery filtered by creation dates within specific timeframes. Validates that customers can find products added within their preferred shopping periods or discover new arrivals. This supports marketplace freshness by allowing customers to browse products created within recent time periods for trend-based shopping scenarios.

Test product discovery using descriptive product tags and product classifications. Validates tag-based navigation where customers explore products by attributes like 'organic', 'handmade', 'eco-friendly', or 'exclusive'. This enables attribute-based shopping experiences beyond traditional category navigation and supports marketplace differentiation strategies.

Validates response includes complete customer profile data with proper JWT token structure including access token, refresh token, and expiration timestamps. Ensures token rotation probability works correctly and new tokens are properly linked to the authenticated customer account.

Test advanced inventory-based filtering capabilities for sellers monitoring stock levels. Validates filtering by minimum/maximum inventory quantities, active status checking, and sorting by inventory quantity. Ensures sellers can efficiently identify low-stock variants requiring restocking and optimize inventory management decisions.
